public_rationale: Amazon's April 20, 2026 announcement and the April 24 Google report identify $5 billion and $10 billion in current investment, respectively [e1, e2]. They also describe up to $50 billion in additional funding, subject to conditions [e1, e2]. Microsoft's November 18, 2025 announcement describes a commitment of up to $5 billion, without establishing payment [e3]. These items do not reconcile $54 billion actually provided during May 19, 2023–May 19, 2026, including $28 billion during April 19–May 19, 2026 [e1–e3]. Epoch estimates that the labs used 15–20% of global operational AI compute at the end of 2025 [e4]. That estimate neither establishes nor refutes a 70% share of Microsoft, Google and Amazon's combined operational compute during January–March 2026 [e4]. The funding totals and compute share remain unresolved [e1–e4].
limitations: No matching capacity-allocation record covers the three companies' combined operational compute in January–March 2026.
No complete payment ledger establishes the claimed funding totals and timing; commitments cannot substitute for completed funding.
Epoch's estimate is tentative and uses a different denominator and period.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: At least 70% of Microsoft, Google and Amazon's compute is dedicated to Anthropic and OpenAI, which the hyperscalers have funded with $54B over three years.

statement.excerpt: Things get even worse when you realize that at least 70% of Microsoft, Google, and Amazon’s compute is dedicated to Anthropic and OpenAI, two companies that burn so many billions of dollars that Microsoft, Google and Amazon have already fed them a combined $54 billion in the last three years

from_speaker: already fed them a combined $54 billion
$28 billion of that coming in the last month
another $50 billion from Google and Amazon
if certain performance obligations are met
our_interpretation: Read the 70% statement as a capacity-weighted share of the three companies' combined operational compute. The wording does not limit the denominator to AI revenue, backlog, or newly added GPUs.
For the ongoing compute observation, use January–March 2026, the latest reportable quarter before publication.
Read 'already fed' as funding actually provided, rather than the maximum value of announced future commitments.
Read the three-year funding window as May 19, 2023 through May 19, 2026, and the last-month window as April 19 through May 19, 2026.
The conditional $50 billion is an observation about outstanding commitments, not a forecast that the conditions will be met.
The target_period covers the explicit cumulative funding window; evidence about compute must additionally match the latest-quarter interpretation.
The metric_scope describes the aggregate funding component. Compute allocation is a separate physical measure.
criteria.support_condition: Matching allocation records show at least 70% of the specified compute dedicated to the two labs, and transaction records reconcile $54 billion actually provided in the three-year window, including $28 billion in the final month, plus $50 billion of separately conditional commitments.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Comparable records establish a compute share below 70%, or a complete funding ledger contradicts a stated total or timing window, or the stated conditional commitments are materially misstated.

evidence.explanation: Confirms one current investment and distinguishes possible additional funding. It is only one component of the aggregate funding claim.

evidence.locator: Opening paragraph; investment terms in the following paragraph
evidence.explanation: The report separates $10 billion invested immediately from $30 billion contingent on performance milestones. Together with Amazon's announcement, this is consistent with the claimed additional $50 billion, but cannot establish the full paid-funding totals.

evidence.locator: Investment paragraph following the Microsoft Copilot discussion
evidence.explanation: Microsoft's amount is described as a commitment ceiling. This announcement alone cannot establish that the full amount had already been provided by the post date; NVIDIA is outside the claimed investor group.

evidence.locator: What happens if frontier labs run out of headroom?
evidence.explanation: This tentative estimate cautions against assuming that the labs dominate all compute. Its global AI-compute denominator and historical date do not match the three-company claim, so it cannot directly contradict 70%.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: Capacity-weighted allocation records for the three companies' combined operational compute in January–March 2026, plus a dated funding ledger for May 19, 2023–May 19, 2026 identifying payments in April 19–May 19, 2026 and separating them from the additional conditional commitments.
